correctness.rationale: Cyclically ordered sampled points generate the polygon hull perimeter as sum of adjacent chords, including collinear cases under the twofold segment-length convention. For any vertex, the nearest enclosing cyclic sample gap (A,B) has joint density N(N-1)/L² (1-(A+B)/L)^(N-2). Let S=A+B and T=A/S: T is independent uniform[0,1], E S=2L/(N+1). The virtual corner loss g_beta(A,B)=S-sqrt(A²+B²+2ABcos(beta)) has exact expectation Lh(beta)/(N+1) using ∫sqrt(c²+s²u²)du. On G=all m edges sampled, the actual chord deficit equals sum of g_beta; on the complement each nonnegative term is at most L, while P(G^c)<=sum_i(1-ell_i/L)^N<=m rho^N. Therefore the stated explicit bound follows, including the rare all-collinear cases. Independently checked angular integral for several beta and a square 10k-repetition Monte Carlo at N=50; observed estimate agrees within its sampling error and must not be mistaken for an exact verification of the exponentially small error term. The all-N proof is the analytic gap argument.

value.rationale: A motivated first-order quantitative approximation of fixed polygon perimeter by boundary-random inscribed hulls, with explicit corner-angle coefficient and an exponentially small uniform-in-N remainder. Unlike volume/area deficit, perimeter has inverse-linear rather than inverse-square scale. The edge-missing correction is mathematically material: ignoring it would falsely claim an exact finite-N identity.

limitations: Requires fixed convex polygon with strictly positive edge lengths and genuine corners; not uniform in families of degenerating edges.
Does not assert variance, limit distribution or smooth-boundary asymptotics.
